heroSubtitle: 28-amino-acid neuroendocrine peptide studied in vascular, gastrointestinal and circadian-signalling models
description: VIP is a 28-amino-acid peptide of the secretin/glucagon superfamily, acting through the class-B GPCRs VPAC1 and VPAC2. It is the standard reference agonist in research on smooth-muscle relaxation and vascular tone, intestinal secretion, and suprachiasmatic-nucleus circadian signalling. Because it is rapidly cleaved in vivo, published protocols commonly compare it with VPAC-selective analogues to separate receptor-subtype effects from clearance effects.

faq.question: What is VIP used for in research?
faq.answer: VIP is used as the reference agonist in VPAC1/VPAC2 signalling studies, smooth-muscle relaxation and vascular-tone models, intestinal secretion research, and suprachiasmatic-nucleus circadian work.

faq.question: What is the CAS number and molecular weight of VIP?
faq.answer: The catalogue lists CAS 37221-79-7 with a molecular weight of approximately 3,326.8 Da for the 28-amino-acid peptide; the sequence is stated on the specification table and on each Certificate of Analysis.

faq.question: Is VIP human or porcine sequence in this catalogue?
faq.answer: The 28-amino-acid sequence listed here matches the human/porcine form, which differ only at position 5 in some species variants. Confirm the exact sequence printed on the COA for your batch.

faq.question: How should VIP be stored?
faq.answer: Lyophilized powder is shipped and stored at 2–8 °C, desiccated and protected from light. Reconstituted solution stability is protocol-dependent and should be established in your own laboratory.
